title: NaFeP: first pairing prediction for an unmade 111 iron phosphide, and the pnictogen-height rule inside one compound
abstract: Companion to arXiv:2609.10614, which built a physics judge that classifies the gap symmetry of a superconductor candidate from its structure and showed that generation in the wire families re-finds the known canon. Here the judge is applied end to end to the single compound that survived its own screen. From 58 iron-pnictide compositions in the electronic window of BaFe$_2$As$_2$ absent from the Materials Project, a zero-cost literature-and-stability screen leaves one with no bulk synthesis and no band-structure, magnetic or pairing calculation: NaFeP (111-type, P4/nmm, Fe$^{2+}$ d$^6$, arsenic-free). The judge, refined with an explicit Stoner gate and a frame-independent symmetry reader, returns a paramagnetic DFT ground state and an s$\pm$ gap: a clean sign reversal between the hole cylinders at Gamma and the electron sheets at the zone corner, at nesting vector (1/2,1/2,1/2), in every basis and cell tried. Whether the gap is nodeless is where the instrument is tested. The phosphorus height (1.16 Å) lies below the empirical threshold of about 1.33 Åseparating nodal from nodeless pnictides, so the structural rule calls NaFeP nodal. The sealed verdict on a metal-only basis said nodeless; a d+p basis that passes the same gates puts the inner hole cylinder at the node threshold (min|g|/max|g| = 0.07-0.10), and a scan of the phosphorus height reproduces, inside one compound, the ingredients of the height rule: a third hole pocket, a switch of the nesting vector to (1/2,1/2,0), a monotonic approach to the Stoner instability, and near-degeneracy of s$\pm$ and d channels beyond 1.33 Å. The prediction we stand behind is the d+p reading: an s$\pm$ superconductor with a near-nodal inner hole sheet, on the LiFeP side of the rule, with the disagreement between bases reported, not resolved by choice. No Tc is asserted; the discriminating measurement, nodal or nodeless, is stated in advance.
summary: This work presents the first gap-symmetry prediction for the unmade iron phosphide NaFeP, classifying it as an s± superconductor. The authors utilize a sophisticated computational 'judge' that tests the material against established structural rules, notably the pnictogen-height rule, providing a detailed, albeit conditional, roadmap for future experimental synthesis.
main_problem: To predict the superconducting gap symmetry for the unmade iron phosphide compound NaFeP using a systematic computational framework.
main_result: The paper predicts NaFeP to be an s± superconductor with a near-nodal inner hole sheet, while also testing the pnictogen-height rule within this single compound.
method: The prediction relies on applying a 'physics judge' pipeline, which incorporates DFT calculations, a Stoner gate, and a frame-independent symmetry reader to classify the superconducting gap structure.
model_or_system: The system is the iron phosphide NaFeP, analyzed using DFT (GGA-PBE, PAW) calculations and a gated Wannier tight-binding model. The analysis compares results derived from $d$-only vs. $d+p$ orbital bases.
key_observables: Superconducting gap symmetry ($s\pm$ vs. $d$-wave), nodal status ($\min |g|/\max |g|$ ratio), and the critical interaction strength ($U_{	ext{crit}}$) from the Stoner gate.
important_parameters: Phosphorus height ($1.16 	ext{ Å}$), empirical structural threshold ($\approx 1.33 	ext{ Å}$), and the nesting vector $(1/2, 1/2, 1/2)$.
main_assumptions: The prediction is conditional on the structural measurement of the nodal/nodeless gap, and no critical temperature ($T_c$) is asserted.
figures_summary: Figures show the Fermi surface colored by gap sign (confirming $s\pm$), the nodal ratio across sheets, and the application of manufacturability gates (F0-F5) along with the pnictogen-height scan.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure of applying a sophisticated 'physics judge' to a single, unmade candidate (NaFeP), detailing the necessary computational refinements (Stoner gate, symmetry reader), comparing results across different orbital bases, and finally testing the structural pnictogen-height rule within the compound itself.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state superconductivity, the rigorous application of advanced computational diagnostics (like the Stoner gate and symmetry readers) to predict emergent quantum phases in novel materials is highly relevant to understanding strongly correlated electron behavior.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks

figures.caption: Figure 1: Confusion matrix read by the frame-independent physical signature (inter-sheet sign structure and nodes) together with the Stoner threshold Ucrit. Five calibration materials and the negative control on the diagonal; Nb and SrRu2As2 separate as null/negative (Ucrit > 2.5 eV). NaFeP is placed in the s± cell as the prediction, not as a calibration point, with both readings (nodeless in d-only, near-nodal in d + p) and both Ucrit values. Calibration accuracy, not a blind test; FeSe hold-out pending.

Figure 2: Selection cascade: 58 Fe analogues absent from the Materials Project →26 novel by the literature gate →5 without a documented chemical wall, sent to the CHGNet formation-energy relaxation →1 stable and unreported (NaFeP). The expensive pipeline is reserved for the single survivor of a zero- cost screen.

Figure 3: Crystal structure of NaFeP (P4/nmm, PBE-relaxed cell). (a) Side view (a–c): Fe–P slabs with Na layers intercalated between them. (b) Top view (2×2): the square Fe sublattice, Fe–Fe = 2.66 Å.
Figure 4: (a) Wannier bands (10 Fe-3d WF) along Γ–X–M–Γ–Z, colored by dominant d-orbital char- acter. (b) Species-projected density of states: Fe-3d makes up 82% of N(EF ).

Figure 5: R5 band-tracking validation of the d-only model on the relaxed cell (frozen window EF −1.8 to EF + 1.5 eV). (a) Wannier E(k) (lines) over the DFT eigenvalues at the 123-mesh points on the path (circles), EF ± 1.5 eV. (b) Residual over the frozen window (12,107 pairs), MAE = 0.015 meV.
